english.title: Three / more persons enter land at night as trespassers to poach armed with a gun / firearm / crossbow / weapon
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being one of three or more persons unlawfully entered or was on land, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LAND..), at night for the purpose of taking or destroying game or rabbits armed with

(A)_[a gun, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GUN..)]_
(B)_[a firearm , namely **(..SPECIFY THE TYPE OF FIREARM..)]_
(C)_[a crossbow]_
(D)_[a bludgeon]_
(E)_[an offensive weapon, namely **(..SPECIFY THE TYPE OF WEAPON..)]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 9 of the Night Poaching Act 1828.

english.notes:
(i) Land includes public road, highway or path and openings from such land (Night Poaching Act 1844).
(ii) "Enclosed" was extended by Section 1 of the Night Poaching Act 1844 to apply to persons destroying game or rabbits on any public road, path, etc.
(iii) See section 2 of the Poaching Prevention Act 1862 for the police power to stop and search persons or conveyance coming from land and seize any game or guns etc.
(iv) See section 2(1) of the Game Laws (Amendment) Act 1960 for the power of entry by the police for the purpose of arresting offenders.
(v) See section 4 of the Game Laws (Amendment) Act 1960 for the police power of search and seizure of game, guns and devices.
(vi) See section 2 for the power of land owner etc to apprehend offenders and deliver to police.
